You are a programming expert. 
You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 

Your task is summarize the modifications made in the patch.
Your summary should consist of two parts, modifications in each file and their relationships.

From e824bbd4d224cce4b5fb59cc9dcd3447fe0b7e44 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: NeilBrown <neilb@ownmail.net>
Date: Mon, 25 May 2026 16:23:45 +1000
Subject: [PATCH] VFS: fix possible failure to unlock in nfsd4_create_file()

atomic_create() in fs/namei.c drops the reference to the dentry
when it returns an error.
This behaviour was imported into dentry_create() so that it
will drop the reference if an error is returned from atomic_create(),
though not if vfs_create() returns an error (in the case where
->atomic_create is not supported).

The caller - nfsd4_create_file() - is made aware of this by checking
path->dentry, which will either be a counted reference to a dentry, or
an error pointer.

However the change to use start_creating()/end_creating() (which landed
shortly before the dentry_create() change landed, though was likely
developed around the same time) means that nfsd4_create_file() *needs* a
valid dentry so that it can unlock the parent.

The net result is that if NFSD exports a filesystem which uses
->atomic_create, and if a call to ->atomic_create returns an error, then
nfsd4_create_file() will pass an error pointer to end_creating()
and the parent will not be unlocked.

Fix this by changing dentry_create() to make sure path->dentry is always
a valid dentry, never an error-pointer.  The actual error is already
returned a different way.

Note that if ->atomic_create() returns a different dentry (which may not
be possible in practice) we are guaranteed (because it is only ever
provided by d_spliace_alias()) that it will have the same d_parent and
so it will have the same effect when passed to end_creating().

Fixes: 64a989dbd144 ("VFS/knfsd: Teach dentry_create() to use atomic_open()")
Signed-off-by: NeilBrown <neil@brown.name>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/177969022571.3379282.16448744624428323496@noble.neil.brown.name
Reviewed-by: Jeff Layton <jlayton@kernel.org>
Reviewed-by: Benjamin Coddington <bcodding@hammerspace.com>
Reviewed-by: Jori Koolstra <jkoolstra@xs4all.nl>
Signed-off-by: Christian Brauner (Amutable) <brauner@kernel.org>

diff --git a/fs/namei.c b/fs/namei.c
index c7fac83c9a85..4787244ca4a7 100644
--- a/fs/namei.c
+++ b/fs/namei.c
@@ -5024,6 +5024,7 @@ struct file *dentry_create(struct path *path, int flags, umode_t mode,
 {
 	struct file *file __free(fput) = NULL;
 	struct dentry *dentry = path->dentry;
+	struct dentry *orig_dentry = dentry;
 	struct dentry *dir = dentry->d_parent;
 	struct inode *dir_inode = d_inode(dir);
 	struct mnt_idmap *idmap;
@@ -5043,9 +5044,18 @@ struct file *dentry_create(struct path *path, int flags, umode_t mode,
 		if (create_error)
 			flags &= ~O_CREAT;
 
+		/* atomic_open will dput(dentry) on error */
+		dget(orig_dentry);
 		dentry = atomic_open(path, dentry, file, flags, mode);
 		error = PTR_ERR_OR_ZERO(dentry);
 
+		if (IS_ERR(dentry))
+			/* keep the original */
+			dentry = orig_dentry;
+		else
+			/* Drop the extra reference */
+			dput(orig_dentry);
+
 		if (unlikely(create_error) && error == -ENOENT)
 			error = create_error;
 
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary of the Patch

### Modifications in `fs/namei.c`

- **Added a local variable `orig_dentry`** to save the original dentry pointer from `path->dentry` before calling `atomic_open()`.
- **Increased the reference count** of `orig_dentry` with `dget(orig_dentry)` before the call to `atomic_open()`, to ensure the dentry remains valid even if `atomic_open()` drops its own reference (which it does on error).
- **Reassigned `dentry`** after `atomic_open()`:
  - If `atomic_open()` returns an error pointer (`IS_ERR(dentry)`), `path->dentry` is restored to the original `orig_dentry` (ensuring it remains a valid dentry, not an error pointer).
  - If `atomic_open()` returns a valid (possibly different) dentry, the extra reference taken earlier is dropped with `dput(orig_dentry)`.
- **Result:** `path->dentry` will always hold a valid dentry after `dentry_create()` returns, never an error pointer, thus fixing the missing unlock in `nfsd4_create_file()`.

### Relationships Between Modifications

All changes are within the same function `dentry_create()` in `fs/namei.c`. They are tightly coupled:

1. Saving `orig_dentry` is necessary to later restore it on error.
2. The `dget()` is needed because `atomic_open()` may `dput()` the dentry on error; without it, the original would be freed and inaccessible.
3. The conditional assignments after `atomic_open()` directly implement the logic: keep the original on error (and drop the extra ref only when success returns a different dentry).
4. Together, these changes ensure that the caller (like `nfsd4_create_file()`) always sees a valid `path->dentry`, allowing proper unlocking of the parent directory even after an `->atomic_create` failure.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
<text>dentry = atomic_open(path, dentry, file, flags, mode);</text>
<text>path->dentry = dentry;</text>
Reason:
When `atomic_open()` returns an error, it drops the reference to the original dentry and returns an error pointer. Assigning this error pointer to `path->dentry` causes `nfsd4_create_file()` to pass an invalid dentry to `end_creating()`, which fails to unlock the parent directory.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
<text>struct dentry *orig_dentry = dentry;</text>
<text>dget(orig_dentry);</text>
<text>if (IS_ERR(dentry))
    dentry = orig_dentry;
else
    dput(orig_dentry);</text>
Reason:
By saving the original dentry and incrementing its reference count before `atomic_open()`, the code ensures that even if `atomic_open()` drops the reference and returns an error pointer, the original valid dentry is restored. This guarantees that `path->dentry` always points to a valid dentry, allowing `nfsd4_create_file()` to correctly unlock the parent directory.
